en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
Sahadhammika-vagga 81.
The Training Rule on the Weak.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying at Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
Now at that time, the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta was assigning lodgings for the Saṅgha and designating meals.
That Venerable One, however, had worn-out robes.
At that time, a single robe had come to the Saṅgha.
Then the Saṅgha gave that robe-cloth to the Venerable Dabba Mallaputta.
The group-of-six monks grumbled, complained, and spread it about,
saying, "The monks are diverting to their own acquaintances property belonging to the Saṅgha."
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires... [and so on]... complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can the group-of-six bhikkhus, having given a robe by a unanimous Saṅgha, subsequently fall into a state of criticism? ... [and so on] ...
"Is it true, bhikkhus, that you, having given a robe by a unanimous Saṅgha, subsequently fell into a state of criticism?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can you, foolish men, after having given a robe by a unanimous Saṅgha, subsequently fall into the state of criticizing it?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:

‘If any monk, after a robe has been assigned by a unanimous Saṅgha, subsequently falls into a state of criticism, saying, “The monks divert to themselves communal gains according to their personal friendships,” it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).’”
"But whoever" means whoever such as this... "monks" means [as previously defined].
...pe... this is the meaning of "bhikkhu" intended here.
A "united Saṅgha" is one that shares the same residence and stands within the same boundary.
"Robe" means any one of the six kinds of robes that is suitable for assignment and is of the last [allowable] size. "Having given" means:
Having given it oneself.
"According to intimacy" means according to friendship, according to acquaintance, according to association, according to having the same preceptor, or according to having the same teacher.
"Belonging to the Saṅgha" means it has been given to the Saṅgha and relinquished.
"Gain" means:
[The requisites] are robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal supplies for the sick; even down to a lump of powder, a tooth-stick, or a thread for a fringe.
To later fall into a state of reproach means:
[to criticize] one who has been fully ordained and appointed by the Saṅgha as a distributor of lodgings, or an assigner of meals, or a distributor of rice-gruel.
If one criticizes [a monk] for giving a robe to the distributor of fruit, the distributor of hard foods, the distributor of minor items, or the distributor of robes,
there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If one criticizes [a monk] for giving a robe when it is a legitimate legal act (*dhammakamma*) and one perceives it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense of *pācittiya*.
If one criticizes [a monk] when a robe has been given for a legitimate legal act while being in doubt about it, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If one criticizes [a monk] when a robe has been given for a legitimate legal act while perceiving it as an illegitimate legal act, there is an offense of expiation.
If one criticizes [a monk] when another requisite has been given, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one criticizes a person who has been fully ordained by the Saṅgha, but who has not been appointed as an assigner of lodgings, a designator of meals, a distributor of rice gruel,
a distributor of fruits, a distributor of fresh foods, or a distributor of minor requisites,
when a robe or another requisite has been given to him, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one criticizes a person who has not been fully ordained— whether he has been appointed or not appointed by the Saṅgha—
as a distributor of lodgings, a designator of meals, a distributor of rice-gruel, a distributor of fruits, a distributor of solid foods, or a dispenser of minor items,
when a robe or another requisite has been given [to him], there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as a legitimate legal procedure, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one is uncertain of it, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as an illegitimate legal procedure, there is no offense.

There is no offense if one speaks in dispraise of someone who, by nature, acts out of desire, hatred, delusion, or fear, thinking: "What is the use of giving to him? Even if he receives it, he will squander it and not apply it properly";
or if one is insane.
"Of the first offender":
the eleventh weak training rule is concluded.
